Gokulanātha_Upādhyāya
(C. 1650-1740 A. D.) of Phaṇadaha (Phanewara) family of Maithila Brahmins residing a. Maṅgalavanī (Mangaraunī); son of Pītāmbara Upādhyāya an. Umā; younger brother of Trilocana an. Dhanañjaya an. elder brother of Jagaddhara; wellversed in Tantraśāstra; patronised by Fateh Shah of Garhwal upto 1699 A. D. an. King Mādhava Sim3ha of Mithila (1700-1739 A. D.); lost his daughter Kādambarī in the Ganges. consequently some of his works are named after her.
--his verses q. in Vidyākarasahasraka p.. 92. 93 (3 verses), 134, 136, 137 (3 verses, one of them from Amṛtodaya; another refers to King Raghunātha. (bhUyaH zrIraghunAthacArukRtinA sphItA punItA babhau)), 138.
See Intro. p. 6.
For details see Umesh Mishra, His.. of Indian Philosophy, II. p.. 373-89; His.. of Navyanyāya in Mithilā, p. 193 ff; Intro. p.. xvi-xvii of Kāvyaprakāśa with G.'s C. Sarasvatī Bhavana Granthamālā 89, Benares, 1961.
